item.title: Delano Smith (feat Diamondancer) - A Message For The DJ (Jimpster Rmx)
item.description: Label: Still Music | Prix: 25,00 € | Style: Deep House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Still Music

Prix: 25,00 €

Style: Deep House

Delano Smith's "A Message For The DJ" was first released in a distant 2005 haze, but the EP has remained a classic ever since. That's because it's a prime example of the combined powers of old-school Detroit techno and more contemporary waves of European deep house; Smith is a master of this artform, and this particular release, out on Detroit's own Still Music, has the ability to please all sorts of listeners and club-dwellers. The lead tune is full-bodied groove, taking inspiration from the US' heritage, but taking the percussion that one bit closer to what many would term 'minimal'. "Inception Dub" is just as classy and laid-back, a dreamy house assemblage with seductive jazzy nuances, leaving main man Jimpster to remix "A Message For The DJ" into a more driving, more charging tech-house monster that is perhaps the pinnacle of the entire subgenre. A piece of contemporary dance music history, right here...

Tracklist:

  • A1. A Message For The DJ
  • A2. Inception Dub
  • B1. A Message For The DJ (Jimpster Red Light remix)

item.title: Rob Pearson - Slipstream (reissue)
item.description: Label: Online Collective | Prix: 20,00 € | Style: Tech House UK Repress
item.content:encoded:
Label: Online Collective

Prix: 20,00 €

Style: Tech House UK Repress

South London's Rob Pearson catches UK tech house in that brief late-90s window where the music still sounded slightly feral, before everything became so polished and deodorised. 'Slipstream' wriggles forward on clipped breakbeats and bulbous sub bass while synth lines bend and smear like heat rising off studio equipment at 4am. 'Vortex' pinches some of Detroit's chrome-plated hypnosis, though Pearson drags it somewhere murkier in temperament. There's a lovely grubby swing to 'Metaphor' too, all bleep motifs and warehouse-house pressure haze. Even the bonus beats version has a rude kind of functionality to it.

Tracklist:

  • A2. Metaphor
  • B1. Vortex

item.title: Chez Damier & Ben Vedren (H2H) - Tonight in Tunisia Remixes feat. Paul Cut; Natalie Nova & Troy Denari
item.description: Label: Recordings | Prix: 14,00 € | Style: House, Deep House
item.content:encoded:

Prix: 14,00 €

A warm Mediterranean summer night. The day’s heat lingers on the walls as the sea breeze carries fragments of conversation into the dark. Time slows, hearts open, and a melody drifts by familiar, yet impossible to place. Minutes later, you’re humming it. This is Tonight In Tunisia... If you know, you know..With these remixes for Re:Imagine, the now well-established pairing of Chez Damier and Ben Vedren continues to blur the lines between deep house tradition and contemporary expression.Built around warm rhythms, sun-drenched melodies, and irresistible vocal hooks, Tonight In Tunisia balances sophistication with immediacy. Rooted in jazzy sensibilities, it offers a version for every mood: open-air dancefloors, late-night terraces, and those summer moments that seem to linger long after the music stops.Effortlessly uplifting and deceptively simple, it’s the kind of record that slips into your mind on first listen and refuses to leave.

Tracklist:

  • A2.H2H Instrumental Mix

item.title: Tony Humphries - Tony Humphries - Running Back Mastermix: The Kiss FM Zanzibar Years (Part two)
item.description: Label: Running Back | Prix: 45,00 € | Style: House , Garage house , New York house
item.content:encoded:
Label: Running Back

Prix: 45,00 €

Style: House , Garage house , New York house

It feels fitting that Running Back's most ambitious 'Mastermix' retrospective to date should focus on garage-house great Tony Humphries and the late 80s/early 90s period in which he was resident at Club Zanzibar in New Jersey and on New York's Kiss FM. There's naturally plenty of high-grade material to be found on this second volume, a triple-vinyl affair that boasts such must-check gems as Jolanda's early US garage classic 'Make My Body Rock', the weighty and stripped-back thrust of Precious's 'Definition of a Track', the pioneering deep bleep of Man Machine ('Electro-Genetik', mixed by Forgemasters), an unreleased, previously acetate-only Kerri Chandler jam, the organ-rich garage-house bounce of The Brotherhood, and a rare, Robert Owens-sporting Chicago house workout remixed by the late, great Ron Hardy (The It's 'Donnie').
